strategy.summary: multipletests on an empty p-value array raises ZeroDivisionError on the buggy revision because alphacSidak and alphacBonf are computed from 1/ntests before method dispatch; the fix guards that computation so empty input returns empty results with NaN corrected alphas. The reproduction is the developer's parametrized test_multipletests_empty in statsmodels/stats/tests/test_multi.py, which must fail on the buggy commit and pass on the fixed one.

statsmodels must be built from source at the buggy commit d3cb403cb5d0 (editable install) so the test exercises the buggy code, not the nightly wheel

strategy.reproducing_test: statsmodels/stats/tests/test_multi.py::test_multipletests_empty (parametrized over sorted(multitest_methods_names)), added by the PR diff: calls multipletests([], method=method), asserts reject.shape == (0,), pvals_corrected.shape == (0,), and np.isnan on alphac_sidak and alphac_bonf.
strategy.success_criterion: Transition: on the buggy revision d3cb403cb5d0 every parametrized case of test_multipletests_empty errors with ZeroDivisionError ('float division by zero') raised inside multipletests before any shape assertion runs, so the test fails; on the fixed revision the call returns empty reject and pvals_corrected arrays, the shape asserts pass, and np.isnan holds for both corrected alphas, so every case passes.
strategy.numerical_probe: multipletests([]) on the buggy commit should raise ZeroDivisionError; fdrcorrection([]) returns empty arrays on both revisions as a control.

input_output_examples.expected_output: empty results (empty arrays); corrected alphas alphacSidak and alphacBonf are nan

risks: Trigger is purely empty input (ntests == 0); no platform, architecture, compiler, BLAS, threading or sanitiser dependence is stated, so the defect should reproduce on any platform with the buggy Python code path, but this is inferred from the code, not from observation.

The test depends on multitest_methods_names being importable from the test module; if the buggy revision's test file lacks that import or the name list differs, parametrization will fail for reasons unrelated to the bug.
Installing the nightly wheel instead of building the buggy commit would test the wrong code; an editable build at d3cb403cb5d0 is required for the transition to be meaningful.
Comparisons against the corrected alphas are NaN-valued, so the test must use np.isnan rather than equality; a fixed revision returning a non-NaN value would fail the assertion.
Exact numpy/scipy/pandas versions are unknown from the evidence; the test uses only basic array and exception behaviour so it should be insensitive to them, but this is not verified.
The installation command uses --use-deprecated=legacy-resolver, which may conflict with a modern pip; the editable source build is the more reliable route.

oracle.reference_source: PR#10013 regression test test_multipletests_empty (shape equality and np.isnan checks)
oracle.why: The pass criterion is a shape match and NaN-ness of the corrected alphas, not a numeric tolerance; no tolerance is stated in the evidence.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On d3cb403cb5d0, multipletests([], method=method) raises ZeroDivisionError from the 1/ntests computation before dispatch, so the call itself errors and the test fails before any assertion.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the guard prevents division by zero, the per-method branches return empty arrays, shape assertions hold, and both alphacSidak and alphacBonf are NaN, so the test passes for every method.
